answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases thus burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the grove deposit is held in the harbor escrow, the beacon audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge burns a deposit of 34 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. The deposit is 48 dollars a seat. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
